messages:
lee: FYI onboarding reranker-v6 with synthetic hard-negatives in candidate set. NDCG@10 went up but MRR@1 dropped ~0.05 on the micro-query slice. Weird tradeoff.

pranav: share slice + exact numbers? hard-negatives often bump NDCG by improving tail rank but can hurt top1 if model becomes overconfident on hard confusers.

lee: slice=micro_multi_short (n=7.6k), candidates=60 (human + synthetic hard negs ~20%). metrics: full NDCG@10 float=0.412 -> hardneg=0.438 (+0.026), MRR@1 float=0.278 -> hardneg=0.228 (-0.050). seed parity ok.

sophia: did you also run the same config but without quant? curious if quant amplifies the effect.

lee: ran both float and quantized (int4 weights + fp16 acts). float-with-hardneg shows NDCG +0.019, MRR -0.031. quant-with-hardneg shows larger MRR drop -0.055. So quant seems to amplify top1 regressions.

pranav: two angles: (A) candidate distribution changed — synthetic negs increase near-ties so top1 sensitivity rises; (B) quant causes small logit noise that flips top1 more often when margins shrink.

sophia: can you dump logit margin histograms (gt minus runnerup) for the four configs: float/no-hard, float/hard, quant/no-hard, quant/hard? that will show whether margins compress.

lee: pasted quick stats: median margin float/no-hard=1.6, float/hard=0.9, quant/no-hard=1.2, quant/hard=0.45. tail(<=0.2) fraction: float/no-hard=4%, float/hard=11%, quant/hard=18%.

eval-bot: run 3301234570 complete. raw numbers as lee posted.

pranav: clear: synthetic hard negs compress margins, especially when paired with quant. Next steps: (1) try calibrating quant with a hard-neg heavy calibration sample, (2) ablate by varying hard-neg ratio in candidates (0%,10%,20%,40%) to find breakpoints, (3) try temperature rescale on logits before softmax as a cheap fix, (4) run loss-aware PTQ that optimizes top1 preservation on a short golden set.

sophia: also test a simple post-score rescaler per-query: linear shrink/stretch to increase margins (tune on dev). If that restores MRR with little NDCG loss, might be easiest short-term.

lee: I'll queue ablations: A=calib-hardneg, B=hardneg-ratio-sweep, C=temp-rescale (T in [0.8,1.2,1.5]), D=loss-ptq-top1. Keeping seeds identical. ETA first batch ~3h.

ops-bot: note: when running hardneg-heavy calibration, ensure batch window and kvpack settings match production to avoid distribution mismatch.

pranav: if (A) helps, add "hard-neg calibration slice" to onboarding. If (C) helps, consider auto-recalibration step in the scoring pipeline for rerankers that used synthetic negatives.

sophia: also flag for product: explain to label/curation teams that adding synthetic hard negatives can reduce single-best accuracy even while improving NDCG; tradeoff needs product decision.

lee: will post compact results {run, MRR@1, NDCG@10, note} when done. Opening a short RFC doc afterwards.

eval-bot: reminder: include random_seeds in each run. float baseline used seed=77.

pranav: thanks — and please include margin histograms in the summary.

sophia: cheers. keep it terse. :)
